about: The class guides (Noah: a guide book for each class that tracks progression, given when the class is chosen). Each class's book is its own chapters, then a live 'Your Progress' page (drawn by the Codex from src/Classes.cpp ProgressNow), then the shared chapters. Paragraphs keep <b> and <i>. tools/gen_esp.py writes the books (BOOK guide_<class>) and src/Codex.h. (Noah: simple but accurate - each class: who you are, your altar, getting stronger, perks, trial and wonder; then three short shared pages.)

chapters.title: The Summoner
paras: A conjurer of the College of Winterhold. Your summons fight for you - every kill they make is yours: Cursed Essence, progress and trials.

You start with Conjure Wolf (left hand), Conjure Skeleton in your spellbook, the Radiant Quarterstaff (right hand) and the Summoner Set (a conjurer's robe, hood and boots) (your armor set: Tier I your summons take a fifth less, Tier II one more summon slot, Tier III your summons' kills heal you). Every class sword climbs the same way: Base is the bare sword; Tier I its element wakes on the blade and every light swing sends out an arc slash in its colour that pierces through the dead; Tier II its heavy attacks burst round where they land; Tier III its own power. The Radiant Quarterstaff's light is white; at Tier III three blades of light circle you and strike the dead that come near.

chapters.title: Your Altar
paras: Your kit - each item with its tier and the price of its next upgrade. Select one to upgrade it.
The Armory - more summon families open as you free cities: Dwemer at 1, Atronachs at 2, the Wild at 3, Ash at 4, Daedra at 5, the Night at 7, the Wrath at 9. You keep every family you buy.
Dragon Priests - every Dragon Priest you slay drops 3,000 Cursed Essence.

chapters.title: Getting Stronger
paras: One curve for everything. Every item in your kit climbs Base, Tier I (1.3 times its damage), Tier II (1.7 times), Tier III - Legendary (2.2 times), then Ascends (+0.3 times each). Prices: Tier I 4,000, Tier II 6,000 (needs 2 freed cities), Tier III 8,000 (4 cities), Ascend 10,000 and 2,000 more each time (6 cities); after night 10 every upgrade and Armory price is 3% higher each night. Your class's armor set is in your kit too: it starts at 5% damage reduction and every tier adds 5% (20% at Tier III), with a power of its own at each tier; each Ascend of the set adds 5% to all your damage. As the set climbs it wraps you in an aura of your class's colour: a faint sheen at Tier I, wisps rising off you at Tier II, a full aura at Tier III, burning brighter with each Ascend.

Summon slots - how many summons you can have out at the same time. You start with 2; the Pack Leader Mead adds one and your robes' Tier II one more - 4 at most. When every slot is full, a new summon replaces your oldest one.

chapters.title: Your Perks
paras: Pack Leader Mead - one more summon out at a time.
Grave Fury Wine - your summons deal 25% more damage.
Bone Burst Brew - a summon of yours that dies explodes, hurting the dead round it.

Up to five brews at once, 3,000 each. They stay through death; select one you hold at the altar to give it back for half. Your class's brews work only while you play this class (they still count toward the five); the seven brews every class can take are in The Echo Altar.

chapters.title: Your Trial and Wonder
paras: Pact of the Host (your city trial): let your summons make the kills - 20 on Novice up to 60 on Legendary.

Soulcaller's Staff (your wonder, a staff): it can't be bought. Once six cities are freed, all four secrets wake - long hidden quests played from altar to altar, never twice in a row in the same city, one at a time (your own class's first). Any class may win and wield any wonder. Listen to the freed altars' whispers. When it is won the Greybeards call: the wonder floats waiting in High Hrothgar's great hall. Hold its cast: its beam tears at the dead along your aim, and each one that dies while you hold it gives the staff its soul (up to six - a pack - counted under your crosshair). Let go and the souls return as spectral wolves that hunt for 20 seconds - one for each soul.

chapters.title: The Battle-mage
paras: A battle-mage of the College of Winterhold: a different element in each hand, struck from afar - bolts, beams, storms and runes.

You start with the Carian Wand (in your right hand - hold its cast and it looses a bolt every half second, fire, lightning and ice in turn; Tier II every 3rd bolt is a great bolt that pierces; Tier III every 3rd also looses a crossing volley; the wand goes steel, stalhrim, glass, ebony, then daedric when Ascended), Ice Spike (left hand), Firebolt in your spellbook, a Destruction tome and the Destruction Set - your armor set (Black Mage Armor's College robes, hood and boots; from Tier I an aura in your class's colour, brighter each tier): Tier I spells cost 10% less, Tier II magicka comes back faster, Tier III spells cost a quarter less. Your magicka starts coming back 1 second after a cast.

chapters.title: Your Altar
paras: Your kit - each element with its tier and the price of its next upgrade: each tier is the next spell of its ladder (Firebolt, Fireball, Incinerate, Immolate).
The Armory - more elements open as you free cities: Shock at 1, Sun at 3, Walls at 4, Arcane at 5, Storms at 9.
Dragon Priests - every Dragon Priest you slay drops 3,000 Cursed Essence.

paras: Overflow Tea - every 3rd Destruction spell you cast is free.
Ember Echo Ale - the dead your Destruction spells kill explode, hurting those round them.
Mana Font Draught - your magicka refills 40% faster.

chapters.title: Your Trial and Wonder
paras: Trial of the Elements (your city trial): kill with two or more elements - 20 on Novice up to 60 on Legendary.

The Staff of Magnus (your wonder): it can't be bought. Once six cities are freed, all four secrets wake - long hidden quests played from altar to altar, never twice in a row in the same city, one at a time (your own class's first). Any class may win and wield any wonder. Listen to the freed altars' whispers. When it is won the Greybeards call: the wonder floats waiting in High Hrothgar's great hall. Hold its beam on the dead to drain them and feed your magicka; where the beam lets go it erupts. Hold it two seconds or more and the eruption leaves an orb of searing light pulsing on everything round it. Hotter still once the three dragons fall.

chapters.title: The Alchemist
paras: A wandering alchemist: flasks of fire, frost, storm, acid, holy water and the void, lobbed into the dead - every flask bursts where it lands, on a body, a wall or the ground.

You start with the Shadowflame Scythe (two-handed - its sweeps set the dead burning with Shadowflame, fire at twice its damage for 5 s; at Tier III the dead that die burning explode and set those round them alight; it grows Forsworn, Falmer, Dwarven, Glass, then Dragon Priest when Ascended), the Fire Flask (sheathe the scythe and your flasks come to hand - attack to throw them, underhand; sheathe the flasks and the scythe comes back) and the Alchemist Set - your armor set (the Gondorian Ranger's cuirass and boots and the Ithilien hood; from Tier I an aura in your class's colour, brighter each tier): Tier I you throw 15% faster, Tier II their bursts reach 20% wider, Tier III each flask kill heals you 2%.
An Alchemist in your party lets everyone mend slowly in a fight.

chapters.title: Your Altar
paras: Your kit - your sword and each flask with its tier and the price of its next upgrade.

The Armory - more flasks as you free cities: the Frost Flask at 2, the Shock Flask at 4, the Acid Flask at 6, Holy Water at 8 (the dead burn in it), the Voidglass Flask at 9 (what it drains comes back to you).
Dragon Priests - every Dragon Priest you slay drops 3,000 Cursed Essence.

Every flask bursts in its element where it lands and leaves a pool of it on the ground. Tier I the burst is half again as wide, Tier II a chain reaction - the dead it kills burst in its element too, Tier III - Legendary a cyclone of its element rises where it breaks and rolls into the dead; Ascends add damage. Flasks cost nothing and never run out - only a breath between throws.

chapters.title: Your Perks
paras: Volatile Tincture - your flasks' bursts reach 25% wider.
Quickhand Elixir - you throw your flasks 25% faster.
Catalyst Philter - the dead your flasks hit take 15% more damage for 5 seconds.

chapters.title: Your Trial and Wonder
paras: Trial of the Crucible (your city trial): kills with your flasks - 10 on Novice up to 30 on Legendary.

The Mutagen Staff (your wonder): it can't be bought. Once six cities are freed, all four secrets wake - long hidden quests played from altar to altar, never twice in a row in the same city, one at a time (your own class's first). Any class may win and wield any wonder. Listen to the freed altars' whispers. When it is won the Greybeards call: the wonder floats waiting in High Hrothgar's great hall. Its orb is fed by six vials of the elements: hold attack to loose a beam that pierces the dead, pouring each vial in turn for 5 seconds; let go and the emptied vials refill.

chapters.title: The Spellsword
paras: A Vigilant of Stendarr: steel in one hand, a touch spell in the other - fire, frost, shock, sun or arcane - that rides every blow of the blade.

You start with the Spellbound Rapier (its element is the spell in your other hand; at Tier III its arcs carry that spell), Burning Touch (left hand) and the Spellsword Set (Black Mage Armor's Black Archmage plate: cuirass, helm, gauntlets and sabatons) (your armor set): Tier I you mend in a fight, Tier II your blade's hits put magicka back, Tier III your blade hits 15% harder. No shields: your off hand is always a spell, and every blade hit casts it.

The Armory - more touch spells open as you free cities: Frost touch at 1, Shock touch at 3, Sun touch at 5, Arcane touch at 7.
Dragon Priests - every Dragon Priest you slay drops 3,000 Cursed Essence.

Spellbinder's Draught - the spell carried on your blade hits 25% harder.
Spellguard Ale - blocking costs no stamina.

chapters.title: Your Trial and Wonder
paras: Trial of Steel (your city trial): melee kills with a spell in your other hand - 10 on Novice up to 30 on Legendary.

Dragon Slayer (your wonder): it can't be bought. Once six cities are freed, all four secrets wake - long hidden quests played from altar to altar, never twice in a row in the same city, one at a time (your own class's first). Any class may win and wield any wonder. Listen to the freed altars' whispers. When it is won the Greybeards call: the wonder floats waiting in High Hrothgar's great hall. It stands two tiers above your blade, and every hit carries the last Spellsword spell you held; once the three dragons fall it grows stronger again, and power attacks loose that spell on the dead round you.

shared.title: How a Night Works
paras: Day (about 20 minutes): the dead sleep. Explore, rest and spend your Cursed Essence.

Night: the dead claw up out of the ground (on open ground, never in houses) in waves - fast runners, more and tougher each night, coming from every side. Each one steps out of the Curse's red portal; elites and bosses out of a larger one. Dawn only comes when the last wave falls.

The night's dead are the curse's whole host, each under its own name: Mihail's zombies and the Thriceborn walk first with the Rag Draugr, rotten skeletons and plague wolves; then Bonemen, the draugr warlords, Draman Brutes, Ash Spawn and werewolves; then the Daedra - Clannfear, Daedroth, Dremora - and at the last the Overlords. None of them cast spells, loose arrows or shout.
From the tenth night the nightwalkers join the waves: feral, and far faster than the rest.

Busy with a quest? Open the wait menu at night, once the countdown has ended, and choose Skip the Night. It passes the whole night to dawn and does not count: no night survived, and the next dusk brings the same night again.

Cursed Essence drops from every kill - spend it at the Echo Altars and the Tablet of Mysteries. After night 10, as the dead grow many, each kill gives a little less. From dusk to dawn a lantern at your belt lights 10 metres round you. At dawn the dead leave their ash where they fell, and in a freed city its people leave an offering at their altar for you each day.
Your health, magicka and stamina sit on one plate at the bottom; its rim glows blue while your shout recovers.

shared.title: The Echo Altar
paras: Every city has one. Step onto it and activate it. Move with the D-pad or W/S, choose with A or Enter, leave with B.

From the top: your class (change it for Cursed Essence - each class keeps its own kit and progress), then sections that open one at a time: Your Kit (select an item to upgrade it), the Armory (new items, opened by freed cities), Perks, Your Dragon, the city's Trials and the Whispers of your path's secret.

Brews (the Perks section): the seven every class can take - Troll's Hide Mead +50 health; Wellspring Draught +50 magicka; Stormrunner Brew you move 15% faster; Bounty Hunter's Ale elites and mini-bosses give twice the Cursed Essence; Last Stand Ale below a quarter of your health you take 25% less; Gilded Tongue Tonic 15% more Cursed Essence from kills; Dragonsblood Cider your shouts recharge 25% faster - and three of your class's own. Up to five at once, 3,000 each, kept through death; select one you hold to give it back for half.

Freeing a city: finish four trials (three shared, one your class's), then slay its Dragon Priest, who rises at night. Its fall ends the night and drops 3,000 Cursed Essence. A freed city is a sanctuary: none of the curse's dead rise inside it. Whiterun gives you a dragon to ride and Dragon's Updraft; Solitude gives you the Dance of Death.
Every 5th night a great boss walks with the dead - kill it before dawn.

Waking an altar: Riverwood's altar is open from the first night. Every other city's trials stay locked until that city's own quest is done - Whiterun: Dragon Rising; Solitude: The Wolf Queen Awakened; Windhelm: The White Phial; Markarth: The Forsworn Conspiracy; Riften: The Book of Love; Falkreath: Ill Met By Moonlight; Morthal: Laid to Rest; Dawnstar: Waking Nightmare; Winterhold: the Jarl's Helm of Winterhold (Dungeon Delving).

shared.title: The Tablet of Mysteries
paras: From the first night an old floating tablet of cracked stone comes down at dusk - in Riverwood first - on a beam of light you can see from far away, and leaves at dawn. Its plinth stays where it stood: look at an empty plinth and it tells you where the tablet is. Hold Activate on it and pay Cursed Essence: its rings grind round and a donated weapon rises out of its face. Hold Activate again within 10 seconds to take it: it goes straight into your hands (what you held goes back to your pack).
Price: 1,500 a turn, and 500 more after every turn or repair, back to 1,500 at dawn; after night 10 it is 3% higher each night.

Used and forgotten: a worn weapon is one tier above your class sword; a battered one (from night 8, 15% of turns - the tablet rings gold) is two tiers above, with fewer uses. Each has limited uses - hits, arrows or casts - shown in its name (62%) and on a bar under your hand cards. Holding it, hold Activate at the tablet and pay a turn's price to mend it to full. At nothing left it breaks; fall and it is lost. You carry one at a time: a new one replaces it.

The mask: after four to eight turns a Dragon Priest's mask may rise instead - your Cursed Essence comes back and the tablet flies to another city, named as it leaves, where it comes down each night until the mask rises again. In a party each player turns their own.

Worn: Stormtalons (claws, 100 uses) - every 3rd hit jumps lightning to 2 more of the dead; a heavy hit stuns the one struck. Gravebell Mace (mace, 100 uses) - every 5th hit tolls it, stunning the dead within 5 m. Riverstone Halberd (halberd, 100 uses) - its hits knock the dead back; a heavy attack splits the ground in a line before you. Cinderclaws (claws, 100 uses) - every swipe sets the dead burning; a heavy swipe flings a fan of embers. Frostmourn Rapier (rapier, 100 uses) - its thrusts slow everything they touch; a heavy thrust freezes a ring of the dead around you. Silver Reaping Scythe (scythe, 100 uses) - every hit on the dead strikes a quarter harder. Wyrmtooth Scythe (scythe, 100 uses) - its hits make the dead bleed; a heavy sweep bursts teeth out of the ground in an arc ahead.

Battered: Rimewick Quarterstaff (quarterstaff, 30 uses) - light hits freeze the dead for 3 seconds; a heavy attack calls a 10 m blizzard for 6 seconds. Talons of Woe (claws, 30 uses) - their bleed runs twice as deep in the dead, and each kill heals you a little. Wyrmspine Pike (pike, 30 uses) - its thrusts pierce through 2 more of the dead in a line; a heavy thrust drives a spike of bone up out of the ground ahead. Eclipse Edge (glass pike, 30 uses) - light thrusts alternate the two; a heavy attack calls a 6-second eclipse that blinds and slows the dead. The Wandering Star (wand, 30 uses) - hold its cast and it looses a star every half second, bouncing on through two more of the dead. Bonereaper (scythe, 30 uses) - one kill in four raises the fallen to fight for you for 20 seconds. Bloodmoon Scythe (scythe, 30 uses) - every hit drains a little of the dead's blood into you; a heavy sweep drains everything it touches.

shared.title: The Road to the Echo
paras: High Hrothgar's hall: once six cities are free, the four secrets wake - your own class's first, then the others, one at a time. Win one and the Greybeards call you - its wonder floats waiting in High Hrothgar's great hall. Look at it and press Activate or left click to take it up. Every wonder answers to every class: mix and match.

The three dragons: with all four wonders won (win each secret in turn, or pool them with your party), Alduin's three words wake as dragons - SLEN at the cult's shrine in the Reach, TIID at Labyrinthian, VO on Mount Anthor. Go at night: the dead come first, then the dragon. Each one slain gives a lasting power, and with all three dead your wonders take their Legendary form.

The Echo of Alduin: last of all, once the three dragons are dead and every Echo Altar is awake, on the summit of the Throat of the World. Slay it and the curse is broken - the nights are only nights again, and High Hrothgar becomes the Hall of the Awakened: Alduin's Bane floats over the fire at the hall's end, and the Endless Flame burning on the centre pillar holds the rest - the First Dragonborn's Regalia, Alduin's Bones for your dragon, the Endless Night and Begin Again (New Game+).

shared.title: Settings
paras: Difficulty is Skyrim's own (Settings, Gameplay) and changes everything - the dead, the elites, the bosses, and your weapons and spells. Novice is very easy, Apprentice normal, Adept hard, Expert very hard, Master extremely hard and Legendary nearly impossible. From Novice to Legendary the dead have 0.6x, 1x, 1.4x, 1.9x, 2.6x, 3.5x health and hit 0.5x, 1x, 1.4x, 1.9x, 2.6x, 3.5x as hard, and your weapons and spells deal 1.5x, 1x, 0.9x, 0.8x, 0.7x, 0.6x damage.
Skyrim's own enemies get tougher with the difficulty and with every altar you free, so they keep up with you.
The Mod Configuration Menu page The Curse of Alduin has the rest: attack and draw speed, field of view, brightness, effects and controls.
